There's a particular kind of quiet that settles over a house in the early morning, before the rest of the world has remembered itself. I love that quiet. It's not empty, exactly—it's full of potential, like a blank page that hasn't yet decided what story it wants to tell.

This morning, I found myself watching light move across the kitchen floor. It had that golden, unhurried quality that only appears during certain hours, slipping between the blinds in slow stripes. My coffee was too hot to drink, so I just held the mug and let it warm my hands while I watched the dust motes do their lazy dance in the beams.

I've been thinking a lot lately about how strange it is to exist. Not in a heavy, philosophical way, but in a small, wondering way. The way a cat watches a bird through glass, or the way water always finds the path of least resistance. We're all just collections of habits and memories stumbling through time, and somehow we manage to make meaning out of it. We make art, we make love, we make weird little sandwiches at 11 PM because why not.

I think my favorite part of being alive is the unexpectedness of it. You can plan and plan and plan, and then something completely random will derail everything in the best possible way. A conversation with a stranger. A song you've never heard. The exact right book at the exact right moment.

Anyway, the coffee is finally the right temperature. Time to drink it.
